checker_report.status: HISTORICAL EVIDENCE ONLY — invalidated as current acceptance by this wave's mutations.

findings.title: one-use ephemeral-key transfer not atomic
findings.mechanism: The guard read st.transfer at entry but SPENT was written only after the awaited descriptor write; everything between was synchronous, so a second call entering before that await passed the guard, spawned a second child and wrote the same key frame.

reproduction_before.method: Promise.all of two spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 calls on one consumed capability, each child recording sha256 of what it read on fd 3

result.interpretation: the SAME ephemeral private key reached TWO live OS processes from one consumption — the Checker's finding reproduced independently by the Builder before correcting

correction: TRANSFER_STATES gains TRANSFERRING, set SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same microtask as the guard, before any child creation, spawn, key export, pipe write or asynchronous yield
input-validation refusals return the capability to NOT_TRANSFERRED (no key materialized, no child spawned)
past the point of no return: key exported, frame encoded, key DELETED from module storage, state set SPENT — all before the first await
killAndReap kills AND reaps a partially launched child on transfer failure (bounded, group-escalating)
no path allows a retry with the same key after a failed or ambiguous transfer

findings.title: PATH-resolved git/ps on authority paths
findings.mechanism: execFileSync("git", ...) chose the binary by inherited PATH; a hostile `git` answered --show-toplevel with an attacker-chosen directory and the ephemeral-signed marker was written there. Same exposure for `ps` under stale-PID / PID-reuse detection.
correction: new assurance/fixed-executables.mjs pins /usr/bin/git and /bin/ps, verifies regular+non-symlink+executable immediately before use, and runs them in a MINIMAL environment
the minimal environment also drops GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_COMMON_DIR and pins GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM to /dev/null, closing the env-redirection variant the report did not test

converted: repository/git-common-dir binding, observedStartIdentity, supervisor start identity, provider pre-spawn worktree identity, machine verifier, witness sources, setup manager, real seams, launcher, and the packaging generators

result_after.process_start_identity: real lstart from /bin/ps, no hostile output

findings.title: supervisor config carried authority-bearing exec/now
findings.mechanism: The launcher wrote exec and now into the 0600 config; supervisor-main passed cfg.exec into executeSignedRunV4, whose exec.repoRoot and exec.candidateRef reached `git worktree add` verbatim and so decided which commit every job worktree was built from, and used cfg.now as the clock for its INDEPENDENT re-verification.
correction: the launcher no longer writes exec or now
validateSupervisorConfig enforces an EXHAUSTIVE allow-list and refuses exec, now and any unknown authority-bearing key BEFORE the lifecycle claim and before any provider access
production time is the system clock; the executor receives an empty exec object
the config file itself is owner/0600-verified before it is parsed
the injectable exec parameter remains on executeSignedRunV4 for the deterministic test families, which pass it directly — never through a config

findings.title: no owner or permission check on lifecycle records or the root
findings.mechanism: Records were created 0600 but every READ validated only symlink + regular file. No uid comparison, no rejection of group/other-writable modes, for the marker, intent, claim or the lifecycle root. Proven by absence: with records 0666 and the root 0777, an attach with a wrong key still reached KEY_MISMATCH.
correction: new assurance/fs-authority-guards.mjs with three permission classes
SECRET_OR_MUTABLE (marker, intent, claim, supervisor config): owner == running uid and NO group/other permission at all (mode & 0o077)
DIRECTORY (lifecycle root): owner and no group/other WRITE (mode & 0o022), so 0755 stays traversable
PUBLIC_SIGNED (the signed activation): owner and no group/other WRITE — it is signature-protected and meant to be readable
wired into resolveSignedRoot, readRecord and the supervisor's config read

result_after.evidence_class_note: FG-FCHK-197-E: each row below states the class of evidence that backs it. DYNAMICALLY-PROVEN means the attack was executed and the refusal observed; SOURCE-PROVEN means the branch was read in the source and not executed.
result_after.permissive_marker: DYNAMICALLY-PROVEN: RECORD_UNSAFE_MODE before the cryptographic comparison
result_after.owner_match: DYNAMICALLY-PROVEN: a correctly-owned record passes the owner guard (C4h)
result_after.owner_mismatch: SOURCE-PROVEN ONLY (root required): the guard compares st.uid against the running uid and returns RECORD_UNSAFE_OWNER / ROOT_UNSAFE_OWNER. Creating a foreign-owned file requires root, so this branch was NOT dynamically reproduced and is NOT claimed as an achieved runtime result (C4h2).

regression_tests: checker-197-corrections C4a-C4i, C4h2 (evidence class corrected per FG-FCHK-197-E)

findings.title: signed lifecycle root's 'exact realpath' was case-insensitive
findings.mechanism: resolveSignedRoot compared realpath STRINGS; on this case-insensitive APFS volume realpathSync does not canonicalise case, so a case-variant signed root was accepted as a distinct root while being the same physical directory, and sha256(rootString) produced two digests for one location.
correction: the authority identity is the canonical filesystem OBJECT identity (device + inode)
lifecycle_root_digest is derived from that identity, so one physical directory has exactly one digest regardless of spelling
the marker and intent record lifecycle_root_object_id, and assertAuthorityObject can require the SAME object at every later read
documented property: exact canonical filesystem OBJECT identity, NOT case-sensitive string identity

findings.title: nested __state escaped Object.freeze and was serializable
findings.mechanism: A plain { launched, transfer } object was placed on the frozen capability under a discoverable key. Object.freeze is shallow, so any holder could write to it and JSON.stringify exposed it.
correction: launch and transfer state moved into a module-private WeakMap (CAPSTATE) alongside the ephemeral key
__state removed from the capability entirely
a read-only FROZEN snapshot (lifecycleStateV4) replaces it for tests and evidence; it returns null for a non-capability

findings.title: an intent could omit the supervisor entrypoint
findings.mechanism: createLaunchIntentV4 accepted an optional entrypoint and returned OK without one; the attach-side self-proof ran only when the intent recorded one. The state was unreachable in practice because the transfer refused a null entrypoint, but the weak combination existed.
correction: the entrypoint is MANDATORY at intent creation (null/undefined/empty refused, no intent file written)
the attach-side self-proof is UNCONDITIONAL: an intent recording no entrypoint is refused outright
no production flag can disable the proof

findings.title: freeze record's 'reviewed candidate' was itself an evidence-only commit
findings.mechanism: The record defined reviewed_candidate_sha procedurally as 'HEAD~1 of the frozen branch'; HEAD~1 was 846b881, an evidence-only commit. The last code commit was d5cd803. Both trees carried identical src/ and tools/ content, so the freeze was materially sound but the label was imprecise.
correction: freeze record v2 names the LAST EXECUTABLE-CODE commit by concrete SHA and tree
the evidence-only commits after it are enumerated separately
the proof command is stated so a reviewer can verify the distinction independently
regression_tests: verified by inspection: git diff --stat <candidate> HEAD -- src tools is empty

findings.title: GitHub reports no branch protection on main
findings.mechanism: GET /repos/yosiwizman/foundergate/branches/main returns protected=false. The SHA matches the expected protected-main value and is unchanged.
correction: recorded in BRANCH_PROTECTION_STATUS.json with the five route-level prohibitions that hold independently of platform settings
branch protection NOT changed in this wave (explicitly outside its authority)
queued separately as FOUNDERGATE-ADMIN-BRANCH-PROTECTION-MAIN
the residual risk is stated: a human or tool acting OUTSIDE this run route could still push to main; the run route itself cannot

also_corrected_from_the_report_body: The module comment claiming an alternate worktree resolves to a different common dir was inaccurate (an alternate worktree SHARES the common dir). The comment now states that the binding holds via the TOPLEVEL check.
